Try executing this chunk by clicking the *Run* button within the chunk or by placing your cursor inside it and pressing *Cmd+Shift+Enter*. 

libraries
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(readxl)
library(writexl)
library(ggplot2)
library(zoo)
```

Overall is to combine the complete set of data from 09/30/2009 — 09/30/2025 (found https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/judgment-fund-report-to-congress/judgment-fund-annual-report-to-congress)
with the incomplete data from 09-30-25 to date

importing the 09/30/2009 — 09/30/2025 dataset
```{r}
data_from_09.30.2009_to_09.30.2025 <- read_csv("JudgFundRprtCongress.csv")
#parsing issues bcs some values are "null" and thus not expected character type
```
importing the incomplete data from 10/1/25- 08/31/26, from
https://fiscalcrm.my.site.com/jfpaymentsearch/s/

NB: in order to download this data you have to select certain 'search fields' (ie departments) which is unforunately inconsistent with
my effort to do all the filtering in the same place (here). 
It also produces 2 files, 1 for claims resolved through litigation and 1 for claims resolved administratively 
```{r}
admin_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 <- read_csv("JFPaymentAdministrativeReport_09-24-2026_122851.csv")
ligi_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 <- read_csv("JFPaymentLitigativeReport_09-24-2026_122844.csv")
```
okay now we have to reconcile these data sets into one giant data set. 

the first step is making sure the variables of each data set match. 
Im changing the variable names to be more usable as well. In principle, I'm mostly changing the incomplete datasets to match the complete set, except that im changing 'confirmed payment amount' to be 'payment amount' in both since some are implicitly not confirmed, and that I use this step to filter out the variable 'record date' which seems meaningless and confusing since it has little relationship with the date on which the payment was made, nor does it seem to be the date on which the lawsuit was filed. see  the judgement fund dataset dictionary for more

```{r}
data_from_09.30.2009_to_09.30.2025 <- data_from_09.30.2009_to_09.30.2025 |>
  select(judgment_type_code = `Judgment Type Code`, 
         defendent_agency_name = `Defendant Agency Name`,
         submitting_agency_name = `Submitting Agency Name`,
         control_number = `Control Number`,
         plaintiffs_counsel_name = `Plaintiffs Counsel Name`,
         payment_id_number = `Payment ID Number`,
         payment_sent_date = `Payment Sent Date`,
         payment_amount = `Confirmed Payment Amount`,
         principle_amount = `Principal Amount`,
         principle_citation_code = `Principal Citation Code`,
         principle_citation_code_description = `Principal Citation Code Description`,
         attorneys_fee_amount = `Attorneys Fee Amount`,
         attorneys_fee_citation_code = `Attorneys Fee Citation Code`,
         attorneys_fee_citation_code_description = `Attorneys Fee Citation Code Description`,
         cost_amount = `Cost Amount`,
         cost_citation_code = `Cost Citation Code`,
         cost_citation_code_description = `Cost Citation Code Description`,
         interest_amount = `Interest Amount`,
         interest_citation_code = `Interest Citation Code`,
         interest_citation_code_description = `Interest Citation Code Description`,
         source_line_number = `Source Line Number`
         )|>
  filter(payment_id_number!="null")|>
  mutate(payment_id_number = as.numeric(payment_id_number))
  

admin_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 <- admin_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 |>
  select(defendent_agency_name = `Defendant Agency Name`,
    control_number = `Control #`,
    payment_id_number = `Payment ID #`,
    payment_sent_date = `Payment Sent Date`,
    principle_amount = `Principal Amount`,
    principle_citation_code = `Principal Citation Code`,
    principle_citation_code_description = `Principal Citation Code Description`,
    attorneys_fee_amount = `Attorney Fees Amount`,
    attorneys_fee_citation_code = `Attorney Fees Citation Code`,
    attorneys_fee_citation_code_description = `Attorney Fees Citation Code Description`,
    cost_amount = `Cost Amount`,
    cost_citation_code = `Cost Citation Code`,
    cost_citation_code_description = `Cost Citation Code Description`,
    interest_amount = `Interest Amount`,
    interest_citation_code = `Interest Citation Code`,
    interest_citation_code_description = `Interest Citation Code Description`,
    payment_amount = `Payment Amount`) |>
  add_column(judgment_type_code = "Administrative")|>
  filter(payment_id_number!="null")
    
liti_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 <- ligi_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 |>
  select(defendent_agency_name = `Defendant Agency Name`,
    control_number = `Control #`,
    payment_id_number = `Payment ID #`,
    payment_sent_date = `Payment Sent Date`,
    principle_amount = `Principal Amount`,
    principle_citation_code = `Principal Citation Code`,
    principle_citation_code_description = `Principal Citation Code Description`,
    attorneys_fee_amount = `Attorney Fees Amount`,
    attorneys_fee_citation_code = `Attorney Fees Citation Code`,
    attorneys_fee_citation_code_description = `Attorney Fees Citation Code Description`,
    cost_amount = `Cost Amount`,
    cost_citation_code = `Cost Citation Code`,
    cost_citation_code_description = `Cost Citation Code Description`,
    interest_amount = `Interest Amount`,
    interest_citation_code = `Interest Citation Code`,
    interest_citation_code_description = `Interest Citation Code Description`,
    payment_amount = `Payment Amount`)|>
  add_column(judgment_type_code = "Litigative")|>
  filter(payment_id_number!="null")

```

combining the data sets into one big data set

```{r}
mega_data<-bind_rows(data_from_09.30.2009_to_09.30.2025, liti_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026, admin_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026)
```

now we have to filter the data to get what's relevant
